description: AI-first reference for Jarvis plugin capabilities. Designed for Jarvis to self-reference when answering user questions about features, workflows, and best practices.

identity.name: Jarvis
core_principles: Git-audited trail for all vault operations
Progressive disclosure — load only what's needed
identity.architecture: modular plugin system with 5 composable plugins

jarvis.description: Core vault management, journal entries, git audit trail, semantic memory, auto-extract, conflict detection, multi-remote sync

jarvis-todoist.description: Todoist integration via official SDK (local stdio MCP, no external HTTP dependency)

jarvis-strategic.description: Strategic analysis, briefings, pattern detection, summaries

jarvis-toolbelt.description: Professional engineering skills and agents — security review, adversarial plan review, TDD workflows

jarvis-obsidian.description: PKM vault workflows — JARVIS protocol git audit trail, journal entries, vault exploration

skills._note: Skills are user-invocable slash commands. Invoke with /jarvis:<skill-name> or just the trigger phrases. 14 user-invocable skills across 5 plugins (plus jarvis-audit, a background reference skill).

jarvis.description: Activate Jarvis identity and load strategic context
jarvis.what_it_does: Checks MCP availability, loads strategic context from .jarvis/strategic/, greets user with capabilities summary

jarvis-journal.description: Create a journal entry with intelligent vault linking
jarvis-journal.what_it_does: Delegates to journal agent to create a timestamped entry with YAML frontmatter, wiki links to related vault notes, and proper categorization. Returns draft for approval before committing.

jarvis-inbox.description: Process and organize items in vault inbox/
jarvis-inbox.what_it_does: Scans inbox/ for unprocessed items, classifies each (journal entry, work note, personal note, contact, Todoist task, discard), presents plan, executes with user approval

review_modes.individual: Review each item one by one (< 5 items)

jarvis-settings.what_it_does: Menu-driven config manager: vault path, auto-extract, vault directory paths, memory system tuning, shell integration. First-time users get a streamlined flow; returning users jump to any section.
jarvis-settings.outputs: ~/.jarvis/config.json with all keys visible (vault, memory, auto_extract, paths)

jarvis-recall.description: Semantic search across vault content using PostgreSQL pgvector
jarvis-recall.what_it_does: Finds related content by meaning, not just keywords. Searches all indexed vault files and memory content. Returns ranked results with relevance scoring.

jarvis-memory-stats.description: Show memory system health and statistics
jarvis-memory-stats.what_it_does: Displays document count, sample entries, per-type breakdowns, and index status.

jarvis-worklog.description: Review auto-captured worklog entries grouped by workstream
jarvis-worklog.what_it_does: Queries worklog entries by date range (default: today), groups by workstream, shows timeline of activities. Can create journal entries from worklog data.

jarvis-schedule.description: Create, list, or cancel scheduled Jarvis actions
jarvis-schedule.what_it_does: Manages recurring Jarvis actions via Todoist. Scheduled actions are recurring tasks with jarvis-scheduled and jarvis-action labels that Jarvis detects during sync.

jarvis-todoist.description: Sync Todoist inbox with smart routing to vault
jarvis-todoist.what_it_does: Checks scheduled actions, loads custom routing rules, classifies inbox items (TASK stays in Todoist with labels, CAPTURE goes to vault inbox), presents summary, commits captures

classification.CLEAR_TASK: Action verbs (buy, call, send, fix) → label and keep in Todoist
classification.INBOX_CAPTURE: Reflection verbs (realized, learned, noticed) → capture to vault inbox/

jarvis-todoist.idempotency: Uses jarvis-ingested label to avoid reprocessing

jarvis-todoist-setup.description: Configure Todoist routing rules and project mapping
jarvis-todoist-setup.what_it_does: Analyzes Todoist projects and tasks, recommends routing rules, creates missing projects (respecting plan limits), saves rules to strategic memory

jarvis-orient.description: Strategic briefing for starting a work session
jarvis-orient.what_it_does: Loads strategic context (goals, priorities, insights), scans last 7 days of journal activity, synthesizes goal progress and open loops, recommends today's focus

jarvis-catchup.description: Cold start briefing after time away
jarvis-catchup.what_it_does: Determines absence period, deep scans all journal entries chronologically, categorizes by work/personal/system, identifies what needs attention, recommends first actions

jarvis-summarize.description: Periodic summary and reflection on journal activity
jarvis-summarize.what_it_does: Parses timeframe (week/month/quarter/year), gathers entries, analyzes themes and patterns, generates structured summary with metrics and reflection prompts

jarvis-patterns.description: Deep behavioral analysis and strategic memory maintenance
jarvis-patterns.what_it_does: Analyzes journal entries over configurable period, detects recurring patterns (behavioral, work, energy), checks principles alignment, identifies ADHD patterns (dropped threads, hyperfocus), offers to update strategic memories

depth_levels.deep: all history, trend comparisons, predictive insights

jarvis-security-review.description: Adversarial security review via dedicated security agent
jarvis-security-review.what_it_does: Delegates to jarvis-security-agent with 4 modes: THREAT-MODEL (design-level), CODE-REVIEW (implementation-level), CONFIG-AUDIT (infrastructure/secrets), CHANGE-REVIEW (PR/diff delta). Auto-detects mode from target type or asks for clarification. Produces structured report with severity-rated findings, evidence, and must-fix checklist.

jarvis-adversarial-review.description: Devil's advocate plan review via external AI CLI in read-only sandbox
jarvis-adversarial-review.what_it_does: Delegates to jarvis-adversarial-agent which invokes an external AI CLI (Codex, Gemini) to stress-test a plan. Supports multi-round refinement (1-5 rounds) where each round builds on previous findings. Produces structured review with findings (severity-rated, round-tagged), counter-proposals, and acknowledged strengths. The external CLI runs in --sandbox read-only mode for safety.

agents._note: Agents are autonomous sub-processes delegated to by Jarvis. Users don't invoke them directly — Jarvis delegates internally.

jarvis-journal-agent.purpose: Create and edit journal entries with vault linking
capabilities: Search vault for related notes and create wiki links
does_not: commit to git — returns draft for approval

jarvis-audit-agent.purpose: Maintain git-audited history using JARVIS protocol
capabilities: JARVIS protocol commits with structured tags
Wiki link following with configurable depth
Git history search (deleted files, previous versions)
Structured JSON results with relevance scoring
jarvis-explorer-agent.respects: File access control policy (asks before documents/, people/)

capabilities: Deep task analysis and optimization proposals

jarvis-security-agent.purpose: Adversarial security review with structured reports
capabilities: Design-level threat modeling with STRIDE reasoning
Implementation-level vulnerability scanning with file:line evidence
PR/diff delta analysis for new attack surface and regressions
Auto-detection of review mode from target type
Structured findings with severity, exploit scenarios, and fixes

jarvis-adversarial-agent.purpose: Devil's advocate plan reviewer via external AI CLI
capabilities: Invokes external AI CLI (Codex, Gemini) in read-only sandbox
Structured findings with severity ratings and fixes
Multi-provider support with automatic binary discovery

mcp_tools._note: Provided by jarvis-core MCP server. 20 tools across 5 categories.

unified_content_api._note: Single entry points for all content operations. Routes automatically by parameter.

jarvis_store.purpose: Write any content — vault files, strategic memories, or memory content (observations, patterns, etc.)
jarvis_store.routing: Provide ONE of: id (update existing), relative_path (new vault file), type (new memory/content)

jarvis_retrieve.purpose: Read or search any content — semantic search, ID lookup, memory read, or listing
jarvis_retrieve.routing: Provide ONE of: query (semantic search), id (read by ID), name (memory by name), list_type (content/memory)
features: Semantic search across all indexed content
include_content flag controls whether document text is returned in list results

jarvis_remove.purpose: Delete content — by ID or strategic memory by name
safety: confirm=true required for global memory deletion

vault_filesystem._note: Raw filesystem operations within vault boundary.

jarvis_file_exists.purpose: Check if file/directory exists in vault

memory_maintenance._note: Index management and health monitoring for PostgreSQL pgvector.

jarvis_index_vault.purpose: Bulk index all .md files in vault into PostgreSQL pgvector

jarvis_index_file.purpose: Index a single vault file into PostgreSQL pgvector (incremental)

jarvis_collection_stats.purpose: Memory system health: document count, sample entries, index status

contextual_summaries_workflow._note: Generation is OUT OF BAND. Indexing, vault writes, and retrieval only READ the summary cache (obsidian.document_context) — no runtime path ever calls an LLM.
operator_sequence: 1. bin/generate_summaries.py  — fill the per-file summary cache (needs an LLM: the OAuth 'claude' CLI on the host, or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the container)
2. jarvis_index_vault(force=true)  — embed the summaries into vault chunk vectors
contextual_summaries_workflow.host_example: cd plugins/jarvis/mcp-server && uv run python bin/generate_summaries.py --vault ~/my-vault --limit 200 --concurrency 4
contextual_summaries_workflow.idempotent: Files whose cached content_hash still matches are skipped without an LLM call; --limit defers the remainder to the next run.
contextual_summaries_workflow.verification: jarvis_index_vault reports contextual_augmentation ('summary' | 'partial-summary' | 'mechanical'), summary_candidates and summaries_used. Anything other than 'summary' means step 1 has not fully landed, and the startup consistency check says so on every boot.
contextual_summaries_workflow.note: bin/reindex_embeddings.py only READS the cache — it can never produce a summary-mode space on its own.

jarvis_resolve_path.purpose: Resolve a named path to absolute filesystem location

jarvis_status.purpose: Get current git status (staged, unstaged, untracked)

jarvis_query_history.purpose: Query JARVIS operations from git log

jarvis_file_history.purpose: Get operation history for a specific file

jarvis_rewrite_commit_messages.purpose: Remove unwanted text from recent commits (REWRITES HISTORY)

cli_scripts._note: Host-side CLI scripts in hooks-handlers/ directory. Not MCP tools — invoked via Bash tool.

path_resolution._note: Resolve plugin directory at runtime. ALWAYS use this — never Glob for scripts.

adversarial_review.purpose: Run adversarial review of a plan using an external AI CLI in a read-only sandbox
adversarial_review.returns: JSON on stdout: {success, provider, rounds_completed (if >1), review: {status, summary, findings[] (with round field if >1), counter_proposal, agreement}}
safety: Working directory confined to vault boundary

multi_round.note: Each round ~1-4 min; subsequent rounds find only NEW issues

memory_system._note: PostgreSQL pgvector-backed semantic memory with dual-schema architecture.

core_memories.description: All memory content — observations, patterns, decisions, summaries, worklogs, strategic memories

vault_documents.description: Indexed vault file chunks for semantic search
vault_documents.persistence: Durable PostgreSQL storage, git-tracked source files

unified_api.description: Three routing tools for all content operations

features.semantic_search: Vector similarity search across all indexed content via pgvector
features.auto_index: Every .md vault file written through jarvis_store is auto-indexed to PostgreSQL pgvector
features.secret_detection: Regex scanner blocks secrets (API keys, passwords) from being stored
features.recency_boost: Recency contributes to the importance score at index time (exponential decay, memory_scoring.recency_half_life_days). There is no query-time recency boost since v3.4.0 — updated_at is the reindex timestamp, not an authoring date.
features.cross_encoder_reranking: Second-stage pairwise reranking using ONNX cross-encoder model (ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2). DISABLED by default since v3.4.0: measured net-negative on retrieval quality (−0.055 nDCG@10 on ArguAna vs the bi-encoder alone). Re-enable only with a reranker that measurably improves labeled nDCG.

conflict_detection.description: Automatic contradiction detection on content writes — supersedes stale entries when new content contradicts them
conflict_detection.exempt_rationale: Worklogs are unique timestamped activity records that cannot contradict each other

hooks._note: Claude Code hooks for passive behavior. Only the core jarvis plugin has hooks.

auto_extract.description: Passively observes conversation turns and extracts behavioral observations into memory

modes.background: Smart fallback: tries Anthropic API first, falls back to Claude CLI

thresholds.min_turn_chars: 200 — minimum total text in a turn to trigger extraction

extraction.focus: User preferences, architectural decisions, workflow patterns, project context, behavioral insights
extraction.output: Observation with importance score, tags, and project context metadata (project_dir, git_branch)
extraction.worklog: Single worklog entry per extraction capturing what the user was working on, categorized by workstream

dedup.observations: Global dedup via pgvector embedding similarity. If the nearest existing observation has raw similarity >= threshold, the new observation is skipped. Configurable at memory.auto_extract.dedup_threshold (default 0.95).
dedup.worklogs: Cross-session dedup via Jaccard word-overlap against last 20 worklogs globally. Prevents redundant entries across sessions for the same workstream. Configurable at memory.worklog.dedup_threshold (default 0.5).

pattern_detection.description: Periodically scans observations for recurring themes and creates pattern:: entries from clusters

pipeline.1_fetch: Query recent observations within lookback window
pipeline.2_signature: Extract token signatures from content/tags/title (stop words filtered)
pipeline.3_cluster: Jaccard similarity clustering into in-memory candidates
pipeline.4_create: Candidates exceeding frequency threshold written as pattern:: entries
pipeline.5_dedup: New patterns checked against existing patterns via Jaccard merge threshold

similarity_threshold.description: Jaccard threshold for merging observations into a candidate

promotion_threshold.description: Min observations to create a pattern from a candidate

max_candidates.description: Max in-memory candidates before LRU eviction

lookback_minutes.description: How far back each scan looks for new observations

merge_threshold.description: Jaccard threshold for dedup against existing patterns

pattern_detection.candidates: In-memory only — lost on restart, re-derived from observations on next scan cycle
pattern_detection.surfacing: Patterns indexed in unified collection, surfaced via jarvis_retrieve and context enrichment (no new MCP tools)

vault_structure._note: Standard vault layout managed by Jarvis. Paths are configurable via ~/.jarvis/config.json paths section.

directories..jarvis/strategic/: Strategic memory files (goals, principles, priorities, insights)
directories.people/: Contact profiles with personal info (ASK FIRST)

core_fields.vault_confirmed: Boolean — must be true for vault operations (required)

secret_detection.description: Enable secret scanning before memory writes

recency_boost_days.description: Legacy key, no longer consumed — recency lives in memory_scoring.recency_half_life_days (index-time importance)

default_importance.description: Default importance score (0.0-1.0) for new memories

postgres_url.description: PostgreSQL connection URL for pgvector storage

pool_timeout_seconds.description: Max wait for a pooled PostgreSQL connection (hook paths use 1.5s). While the database is down a circuit breaker fails calls immediately and retries every ~10s

min_turn_chars.description: Minimum text in a turn to trigger extraction

max_transcript_lines.description: Max new lines to read from transcript per invocation

dedup_threshold.description: Raw cosine-similarity threshold for observation dedup. Higher = stricter (fewer false positives). Lower = catches more duplicates. Scale: -1.0 to 1.0; 1.0 is identical direction.

enabled.description: Master switch for automatic vault memory injection on every user message

threshold.description: Minimum raw cosine similarity for injection. The 2026-07-17 calibration measured 0.876 as the zero-false-positive point, but recall there was only 0.26 (most prompts injected nothing); 0.85 is the recall-favoring operating point (recall ~0.58, ~16% off-topic leak per labeled data). Raise toward 0.876 for precision, lower toward 0.80 for recall. Importance boosts never rescue an off-topic match. Proper recall fix is the planned reranker, not a looser cutoff.

budget.description: Total character budget for injection (3-way split: local/vault/remote when remote schemas present, otherwise 50/50 local/vault; unused budget overflows to other buckets)

max_results.description: Maximum memories injected after thresholding, ranking, and deduplication. The character budget may reduce this further.

debug.description: Enable debug logging for context enrichment

passive_retrieval_increment.description: Fractional retrieval_count bump per passive surfacing (0=disabled, 0.01=default, 1.0=same as explicit recall)

schemas.description: Which schemas to search: 'all' (default), 'local', 'obsidian', or comma-separated (e.g. 'local,remote_personio')

enabled.description: Persist score-only semantic retrieval traces without changing live selection

store_user_prompts.description: Store full user-facing prompts; internal document-derived searches remain hash/reference only

candidate_detail_limit.description: Maximum candidate locator/score rows stored per retrieval

shadow.description: Durable host-BGE shadow scoring controls; shadow results never mutate live retrieval policy

enabled.description: Enable markdown heading-based chunking for per-section embeddings

min_chunk_chars.description: Minimum chunk size before merging with adjacent chunk

max_chunk_chars.description: Maximum chunk size before paragraph splitting

heading_levels.description: Which heading levels to split on

contextual_embeddings.description: Prepend a 'Document: <path> — <title> › <heading>' prefix when embedding/reranking fragments (stored text unchanged). Rollback switch; changing it requires jarvis_index_vault(force=true)

contextual_summaries.description: One LLM-written situating sentence per FILE, cached in obsidian.document_context and added to the prefix so relational queries ('goals my manager Igor gave me') can match. Keys: enabled, model, max_chars (bounds generation AND the prefix line), body_excerpt_chars, max_generations_per_run, concurrency, timeout_seconds. Generation is OUT OF BAND — run bin/generate_summaries.py, then jarvis_index_vault(force=true); the cap/concurrency/timeout keys are that script's defaults. Changing 'enabled' changes the embedding space

enabled.description: Enable importance scoring from content signals

recency_half_life_days.description: Exponential decay half-life for recency boost

enabled.description: Enable rule-based query expansion with synonyms and intent detection

max_expansion_terms.description: Cap on added terms per query

enabled.description: Enable cross-encoder reranking for explicit recall and context enrichment. Disabled by default until a reranker backend is configured.

backend.description: Reranker inference backend. Host mode uses a native llama.cpp-compatible service.

candidate_count.description: How many results to over-fetch from pgvector for reranking

top_k.description: Legacy reranking cap; the caller's n_results decides the final result count

max_latency_ms.description: Latency budget — if exceeded, falls back to vector scores

batch_size.description: Tokenization batch size for ONNX inference

host_url.description: Native reranker service URL used by the host backend

dedup_threshold.description: Jaccard word-overlap threshold for cross-session worklog dedup. Checked against last 20 worklogs globally. Higher = stricter (1.0 = identical). Lower value catches more near-duplicates.

enabled.description: Enable observation staleness detection based on file modification times

penalty.description: Relevance score penalty applied to observations whose tracked files have changed since capture

enabled.description: Enable background pattern detection from observations

similarity_threshold.description: Jaccard threshold for merging observations into a candidate

promotion_threshold.description: Min observations before creating a pattern from candidate

max_candidates.description: Max in-memory candidates before LRU eviction

lookback_minutes.description: How far back each scan looks for new observations

merge_threshold.description: Jaccard threshold for dedup against existing patterns

todoist_prompt_alerts._note: Config path: todoist.prompt_alerts. Background sync loop fetches tasks from Todoist REST API and writes a local JSON cache. The UserPromptSubmit hook reads the cache (~3ms) to inject <todoist-alerts> blocks alongside vault memories.

enabled.description: Master switch for Todoist prompt alerts (opt-in)

max_per_category.description: Max tasks shown per alert category in hook output

api_timeout_seconds.description: HTTP timeout for Todoist API calls

alert_categories.overdue: Tasks with due date before today
alert_categories.due_today: Tasks due today (excluding overdue timed tasks)
alert_categories.inbox_unprocessed: Inbox tasks with no labels (raw captures)

paths._note: All vault-relative paths are configurable. Use jarvis_resolve_path to resolve at runtime.

shell_integration.executable: Standalone jarvis.sh script installed to PATH (e.g. ~/.local/bin/jarvis); install.sh refreshes it (with a backup) on every run
shell_integration.env_var: __JARVIS_CLAUDE_STATUSLINE__=1 enables gold JARVIS indicator in statusline
shell_integration.behavior: Every probe is time-bounded and the launcher always ends in `exec claude`, even when Jarvis, PostgreSQL or Docker is down; it prints one stderr line saying why memory is degraded

docker.description: MCP server runs in Docker container, connects via HTTP
docker.bind_host: MCP ports are published on 127.0.0.1 unless server.auth.enabled is true (JARVIS_BIND_HOST=0.0.0.0 in the repo compose); the explorer is always loopback
docker.health: GET /health is always HTTP 200 with status 'ok' while the server answers; postgres.status (ok|recovering|unreachable|disk_full|unknown) is the cached database state
docker.backup: plugins/jarvis/scripts/jarvis-transport.sh backup [N] writes a verified pg_dump to ~/.jarvis/backups (dir 700, files 600, other *.dump there tightened to 600) and keeps the newest N (default 7); JARVIS_COMPOSE_FILE overrides the compose file
docker.note: Plugin install still required for skills, agents, and MCP instructions. Docker is the standard deployment method.

maximize_value: Journal frequently — the more entries, the better patterns/summaries become
Use orient at session start to stay aligned with goals
Let Todoist be the quick capture tool, vault be the knowledge base
Run pattern analysis monthly to spot behavioral trends
Keep strategic memories updated — they're Jarvis's long-term context at .jarvis/strategic/
Use specific entry types (incident-log, learning, idea) for better categorization
Use /jarvis-recall for semantic search — finds related content by meaning, not just keywords
Auto-extract passively captures observations from your conversations — review with /jarvis-memory-stats
Worklog entries auto-track what you work on — review with /jarvis-worklog to see your day's activity
performance: Jarvis delegates to sub-agents to preserve main context window
Journal and audit agents use Haiku (fast, cheap) — Todoist uses Sonnet (needs reasoning)
Explorer agent handles vault searches so main context stays clean
Shell integration (jarvis command) auto-loads identity without /jarvis:jarvis skill
Vault files are auto-indexed when written through jarvis_store — for manual additions, ask Jarvis to reindex
Auto-extract runs in background with per-session watermarks — zero impact on conversation speed, no re-processing
gotchas: vault_confirmed must be true in config or vault writes will fail
Shell integration needs restart after install (source ~/.zshrc or new terminal)
JARVIS protocol commits don't use Co-Authored-By — they use protocol tags
Sensitive dirs (documents/, people/) require explicit user permission per access
Todoist uses jarvis-ingested label for idempotency — don't remove it manually
PostgreSQL upsert merges JSONB metadata — to fully replace, delete then re-add
Observations get project context (dir, branch) automatically via the Stop hook
